prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control (CBTC): underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering. Operations Control Centre: Line Traffic Controller monitors trains/routes/alarms/performance; assesses passenger impact/downstream recovery before holding/skip-stop/turnback/run-through. Metro Operations Control System (Lantern) sends Crew Login Token Bundle; displays options from timetable/dwell/headway/route availability, proposed action/train identities/recovery before confirmation; nonvital. Revenue Train Operator owns readiness/compliance. Service Timetable Server supplies schedules; Passenger Information Gateway distributes approved messages; outputs protection-isolated. Voice Dispatch Console cannot replace safety messaging/validation. North District Zone Controller (Marble): northern mainline/turnback/East Junction Interlocking (Falcon) approach. South District Zone Controller (Orchid): southern mainline/turnback/West Junction Interlocking approach. Zones constrain authority, preserve separation/locking, report conflicts/unavailability. Interlockings send vital point/occupancy/locking states; retain point/locking/release authority. Authority requires proved/locked points, overlap/flank protection, conflict locking; boundaries require route/points/vacancy. Mismatches restrict authority; lost correspondence withdraws/shortens within braking envelope. Detection/correspondence/opposing-route criteria govern release. Conflicting axle-counter evidence resolves restrictively. Falcon sends Axle Counter Reset Request; locked routes/approaching trains inhibit reset. Maple (unidentified) verifies/records clearance before restoration. West sends Route Release Exception List; zones retain hazard until path excluded; indications distinguish delay/fault. Atlas Onboard Controller (Kestrel): initialization/protected-manual/automatic/fallback/cutout; validates authentication/integrity/token context; rejects stale/inconsistent messages; enforces authority/speed/doors/vehicle/braking; reports rejection/degradation; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log. Dual Channel Odometer supplies independent speed/distance; divergence degrades/increases separation. Transfer requires onboard position and receiving-zone route/identity/track validation. Vehicle isolation/brake-feedback assurance required. Train Radio Modem reports bearer/registration/continuity; sequence/timeouts validated. Wayside Radio Access Network (Saffron): overlapping coverage, preferably make-before-break; sends Radio Handover Audit File; coverage/handover/capacity monitored. Loss may require holding; degradation uses last validated authority. Safety Data Communication Network: segregated/authenticated/integrity-protected deterministic vital messaging; sends Clock Drift Sample Report; persistent faults

New part:
S117: The Voice Dispatch Console is used when direct verbal instruction is required, and the instruction is repeated back by the Revenue Train Operator before the action is treated as accepted.
S118: The Revenue Train Operator reports train condition, cab indications, passenger issues, and any local hazard that cannot be confirmed from the control room display alone.
S119: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server provides non-vital trend data that helps the Signal Maintenance Engineer determine whether an incident has an equipment cause or an operational cause.
S120: The Signal Maintenance Engineer advises the Line Traffic Controller on equipment recovery options, but the Line Traffic Controller remains responsible for service regulation decisions during the event.
S121: The Service Timetable Server is updated only through an approved timetable change workflow, and the Line Traffic Controller verifies that the revised plan is visible before relying on it for regulation.
S122: The Passenger Information Gateway receives the operational service state needed to align platform messages and train destination information with the current regulating plan.
S123: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance uses the sample report to verify that certificate validity windows and controller clocks remain within the permitted tolerance before operational use.
S124: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance produces the Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack under an approved maintenance window and records the change reference for later security audit.
S125: The Cyber Security Officer reviews certificate change records, access events, and unusual authentication failures before authorising normal operational reliance on the renewed security configuration.
S126: Authority review is performed after major incidents, degraded operations, and timetable interventions to confirm that each commanded movement remained consistent with interlocking state, controller intent, and recorded train response.
S127: This section describes the operational interfaces between the Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System and station equipment that affects departures, passenger information, and dispatcher awareness.
S128: Platform equipment is treated as part of the movement-authority environment when its state can prevent a train from arriving, dwelling, or departing safely.
S129: Platform Screen Door Controller produces the Platform Door Status Snapshot at each monitored platform face for operational use by the CBTC system.
S130: The door interface reports closed, locked, bypassed, inhibited, and faulted conditions using coded states that are interpreted consistently across the line.
S131: A departure command is not considered available to the Revenue Train Operator until the relevant platform door state is compatible with the requested direction of travel.
S132: North District Zone Controller suppresses platform departure authority when the associated berth reports an unsafe door interface state.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
